title: fix(metadata): FilesystemLoader remembers what findFile resolved, so a repeated read makes no fs.access probe
body:
Fixes #24537
Clause-②: no

## What changed

`FilesystemLoader` (`packages/metadata/src/loaders/filesystem-loader.ts`) now remembers what `findFile` resolved for each `(type, name)`. The answer is either the path or "no file". The memo belongs to one loader instance, so each kernel has its own. A repeated read of the same name makes no `fs.access` probe, whether a file holds the name or not.

- The caller is `plugin-security`'s `catalogSetLoader` (`security-plugin.ts`). It does not change.
- The fix lands where the claim expected. The loader is the producer of the cost, and no other package changes.
- Nothing public is added: no member, export or option. In the emitted `dist/node.d.ts`, `FilesystemLoader` gains only `private` members, and its public members are byte-identical.

## Premise, measured before any change (`origin/main` 2667e2402)

The probe counted calls to `node:fs/promises.access` along the real chain:

`createSecurityCatalogReader().resolve('permission', name)` → `NodeMetadataManager.getDiagnosed` → `FilesystemLoader.load` → `findFile`

It used the plugin's format set (yaml, json, typescript, javascript), which makes five resolvable extensions.

| name | `fs.access` per resolution, over 4 resolutions |
|---|---|
| no file holds it | 5, 5, 5, 5 |
| `permission/hit_set.json` holds it | 2, 2, 2, 2 (`load` and `stat` each resolved it) |

One narrowing of the card's reach: only names that the engine registry does not serve fall through to the metadata service. A set the registry holds never reaches this loader. That covers platform sets, the sets in package manifests, and environment-authored sets hydrated from `sys_metadata`.

The same probe after this change reads `5, 0, 0, 0, 0` for the miss and `1, 0, 0, 0, 0` for the hit.

## What can change the answer, and what retires it

I enumerated every in-process path that touches `ROOT/TYPE/`:

| path | exists? | how the memo is retired | pinned by |
|---|---|---|---|
| `FilesystemLoader.save()`, the only in-process writer. It is reached through `MetadataManager.save()`, which no production code in this repo calls. | yes | Every entry is retired, in a `finally`, because a direct write can fail after creating the file. | "a save through the loader retires a remembered miss" |
| `FilesystemLoader.delete()` | does not exist | n/a | n/a |
| The file watcher on `added` / `changed`. This is `NodeMetadataManager.handleFileEvent` (chokidar), which runs only with `watch: true`. | yes | The handler already re-reads with `useCache: false`. That read now resolves the name again from disk and keeps the answer. | "an `added` file event ..." |
| The file watcher on `unlink` | yes | The handler reads nothing. The next read finds the remembered path gone: `stat` reports ENOENT/ENOTDIR, or the probe that `exists()` makes to confirm the path fails. That read resolves the name once more from disk and logs no stat failure. | "an `unlink` event ..." |
| The loader's own walk (`list`, `loadMany`, `loadManyKeyed`, all through `resolvableNames`) | yes | that type's entries | the RECORD case |
| Artifact reload (HMR POST or the artifact watcher), and `register()` | yes | Not needed. Both write the manager's registry, which `get` / `getDiagnosed` ask before any loader. | the two "writing a permission set" cases |
| The ADR-0008 `FileSystemRepository` | It writes under `ROOT/.objectstack/metadata`, never under `ROOT/TYPE/`. | n/a | n/a |

Two more guards:

- **Race.** A probe can still be on disk when a retirement happens. An epoch counter stops it from writing its older answer back. Pinned by "a probe that was on disk ...".
- **Bound.** Callers supply the names, so the memo is capped at 10,000 entries and starts over past that. Pinned by "is bounded ...".

## The gap no event reaches

The gap is named here and deliberately not closed with a clock. The scenario:

1. A name has already been answered "no file".
2. Another process then creates `ROOT/TYPE/NAME.ext`.
3. No watcher is running.

No watcher running is the normal case: every shipped composition passes `watch: false`. That covers `createStandaloneStack`, both of `os serve`'s doors (the dev artifact door and the host-config door), and the verify harness.

- **On main today.** `get()` sees the file on the next read, because `findFile` probes every time. `list()` sees it once the manager's 30 s list cache expires and the next `list()` walks.
- **After this PR, `list()`.** Unchanged.
- **After this PR, `get()`.** It keeps the remembered miss until one of three things happens: the next walk of that type (the next `list()` after the TTL is one), a `save()` through the loader, or a restart. A walk retires the type, so `get()` is never staler than `list()`. A name that `list()` reports is never answered `null`.
- **Edits to a file that already resolves.** These are still read on the next request, because the content cache revalidates by etag. Pinned by the CONTROL case.
- **Deletions.** These are covered by the `unlink` row above.

The gap is pinned as a `RECORD:` case, so any change to it shows up in a diff.

## "Activating or writing a permission set is seen on the next request"

Neither of these goes through this loader:

- **Activation.** `POST /security/_activation/:type/:name` (`packages/runtime/src/domains/catalog-activation.ts`) writes a `sys_metadata_activation` row. The resolver reads that ledger (`readDisabledCatalogNames`), not the catalog body, so the memo never sees it.
- **Writing a definition.** `saveMetaItem` (the clone door, for example) puts the set in the engine registry through `registerItem`, and `catalog.resolve` asks that registry first. `MetadataManager.register()` puts it in the manager's registry, which `getDiagnosed` asks before any loader.

Two cases pin that a remembered miss hides neither write.

## Tests

`packages/metadata/src/loaders/filesystem-loader-resolution-memo.test.ts` has 13 cases. They run real files in a tmpdir through the real `NodeMetadataManager` and the real `createSecurityCatalogReader`, and count probes at `node:fs/promises.access`.

- probe count, miss: `[5, 0, 0, 0, 0]`
- probe count, hit: `[1, 0, 0, 0, 0]`, and the body is still served
- CONTROL: an edit to a resolved file is read on the next resolution
- two managers do not share what they remember
- a set written to the engine registry is seen on the next resolution
- a set registered with the metadata service is seen on the next resolution
- a save through the loader retires a remembered miss
- an `added` file event announces the body (not `null`), and the next resolution sees the file
- an `unlink` event: `load()` and `exists()`, each asked first, answer the miss, and no stat failure is logged
- a deletion no event reports is re-resolved from disk (json removed, yaml added → the yaml body)
- RECORD: the gap above, closed by the next walk
- a probe still on disk during a save does not write its miss back
- the memo is bounded

Results on the final head (HEAD dff1e3f72):

- `pnpm --filter @objectstack/metadata test`: 64 files, 905 tests, all passed.
- `pnpm --filter @objectstack/metadata typecheck`: exit 0. `tsc --listFiles` includes the new test file.

## Ablation

There is one leg per mechanism. Each leg ran through `scripts/ablation-replace.mjs` in WRAP mode: the anchor hit once, the mutation was proven on disk by blob hash, and the restore was proven (blob equals HEAD, `git diff HEAD` empty). The test imports `./filesystem-loader.js` relatively, so it reads source and no `dist/` step applies.

| leg | mutation | went red |
|---|---|---|
| memo | `if (remembered?.has(name))` → `if (false && …)` | both probe counts, the RECORD case, the bound (4) |
| save retire | `this.retireResolutions();` → `void 0;` | the save case, the late-probe case (2) |
| walk retire | `this.retireResolutions(type);` → `void type;` | the RECORD case (1) |
| fresh read | `resolveStats(type, name, !useCache)` → `false` | the `added` event case (1) |
| self-heal | the ENOENT/ENOTDIR `continue` → `if (false)` | the `unlink` case, the unreported-deletion case (2) |
| `exists()` confirmation | the fresh fallback → `return true` | the `unlink` case (1) |
| epoch | `if (epoch === this.resolutionEpoch)` → `if (true)` | the late-probe case (1) |
| bound | the cap test → `if (false)` | the bound case (1) |

## Gates

The local subset was derived with `node scripts/pm/dispatch-gates.mjs --commands --repo objectstack-ai/objectstack` from the real diff, on the final head dff1e3f72 (merge base 5a871e4e4). It produced 64 commands, and I ran all of them.

- Each exit code was captured before any pipe. **All 64 exited 0.**
- `--ran` reconciliation: `64 derived, 64 run, 0 NOT-MEASURED, 0 UNRUN` ("a DERIVED zero — all 64 recorded an exit code and none of them is 3").
- An earlier run, before merging main (6fb0a2d6b), hit three prerequisite refusals (exit 3), all since cleared:
  - the plugin-teardown self-test could not reach its pinned fixture commit from the shallow clone;
  - `check:lean-entry-closure` needed `@objectstack/objectql`'s built dist;
  - `check:dual-build-cjs-loads` needed built dist for every package.
  All three exit 0 on the rerun at dff1e3f72. Its last line reads: 111 require entry points across 69 packages load.
- After the merge I rebuilt `@objectstack/spec`. `check:generated` reported all 14 generated artifacts up to date.
- Left to CI and read from this PR's check-runs, not re-run locally: the required contexts (`Lint & Repo Gates`, `TypeScript Type Check`, `Test Core`, `Build Core`, `Governed Surface Queue Guard`). `test:repo` was not run locally either: the diff touches no file in that project.

## Acceptance notes

- **Not filed, no owner yet.** Artifact-mode runtimes still register this `FilesystemLoader` at `rootDir`. `NodeMetadataManager` installs it whenever no loaders are passed, and `MetadataPlugin` never passes any. Two pieces of documentation disagree with that: `MetadataPluginOptions.watch` says the source-file scan is redundant in artifact mode, and the `bootstrap: 'artifact-only'` branch says "Never touch the filesystem". The per-request probe this PR memoises exists only because that loader is registered. Removing it from artifact modes would be a composition change with its own blast radius. I took no public-door reading, so it is noted here rather than filed.
- **Observation.** A name that a file does hold still costs one `fs.stat` and one `readFile` per read. That is the content cache's etag revalidation, and it is what keeps edits visible without a watcher. It only applies when a file exists under the root, so it is not the miss path this card measured.
- **Observation.** `FilesystemLoader.contract` declares `supportsWatch: true`, but the loader has no watch of its own: `NodeMetadataManager` owns the chokidar watcher. That is why the watch retirement rides on the handler's existing `useCache: false` re-read and the read-time repair, and not on a new loader member.
